tasting_notes: Pungent green anise and liquorice nose; rich anise palate, bone dry with fennel and herbal complexity, soft liquorice, minty lemon freshness; long herbal liquorice finish.
Post-absinthe-ban anise spirit flavoured with star anise, fennel and herbs; lighter, slightly sweeter and more aromatic than the Marseille style. Wormwood-free (distinct from Pernod Absinthe).
Launched 1951; Mediterranean-inspired blend of Chinese star anise, herbes de Provence, liquorice, fennel and cola nut. A softer, more delicate style popular around Marseille.
Colourless white pastis dominated by star anise, no added caramel; turns opaque white with water. Cleaner and less liquorice-forward than yellow pastis.
The yellow counterpart to Berger Blanc; classic golden anise-and-liquorice pastis with caramel colouring, rounder and sweeter on the palate than the Blanc.
Corsican-origin pastis (created Bastia 1925); distilled from green anise and badiane then infused with liquorice. Straw-yellow with light floral aroma and fresh green-anise flavour.
Grand Cru artisanal pastis built on 65+ Provençal plants and spices (thyme, rosemary, savory, sage, cinnamon, cardamom). Complex, layered, herbal; deliberately low liquorice to let botanicals show.
Henri Bardouin recipe enriched with four rare ingredients: vetiver, Forcalquier saffron, Centifolia rose and Sichuan pepper. Bright saffron colour; floral rose-led nose, spicy structure, long finish.
Azure-blue Pastis de Marseille built on badiane essence, liquorice and a touch of wormwood, with grey pepper, grains of paradise, nutmeg, clove and mace. Aniseed nose evolving to spicy finish.
Maceration-made Provençal pastis assembling wormwood, spices and liquorice macerated at least three weeks. The house's classic bar-style pastis.
Azure-blue pastis softened with liquorice; fresh star-anise attack with good length. Janot claims to be the first house to release a blue pastis.
Certified-organic version of the Janot traditional recipe, served diluted 6-8 parts water. Same maceration method with organically grown plants.
Hand-made Marseille pastis from plants sourced at the historic Herboristerie du Père Blaize, macerated in organic surfin alcohol. Star anise and liquorice lifted by Provence fennel.
More complex second cuvée adding aromatic herbs (verbena, pepper, yerba mate) to green anise and star anise. Herbaceous, layered, less conventional than the N°1.
Vintage-dated artisanal pastis from fresh estate-grown plants macerated in fine alcohol; reflects seasonal variation, vatted 6-10 months.

spirit_name: Pastis Château des Creissauds XO 6 ans (Millésimé 2015)
tasting_notes: Estate pastis aged 6 years in a Tokay barrel, giving rounded notes and concentrated aromatics. Barrel-ageing is unusual for pastis.
Green-anise-and-liquorice pastis rounded out with Provençal plants; cuvée named in tribute to the Foreign Legion's white kepi.
Loire Valley pastis on star anise plus 15+ plants and spices, no added caramel (natural off-white colour). Subtle nose of liquorice, cardamom and pepper; fine, stimulating finish.
Organic pastis from double-distilled star anise, liquorice and local fennel seed; intense, fresh aromatic bouquet. Made at the historic Isère liqueur house (est. 1872).
